title: Brock Purdy Shines in Mexico City Victory, Boosting 49ers‑Vikings MVP Talk – Live Updates
body:
San Francisco’s quarterback Brock Purdy delivered a masterclass performance on Sunday night, guiding the 49ers to a decisive 35‑10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings at Mexico City’s Estadio Banorte. The win not only solidified San Francisco’s early‑season dominance but also added significant weight to Purdy’s burgeoning MVP conversation, as he posted a flawless 22‑for‑22 passing line, three touchdowns and zero interceptions in front of a roaring international crowd.

The 49ers arrived in Mexico City after a dominant 41‑10 rout of the Detroit Lions, and they continued that momentum with a balanced attack that blended precision passing with a bruising ground game. After a 10‑0 early lead, the 49ers struck quickly in the second quarter, with Purdy connecting on a 44‑yard strike to wide‑out Deebo Samuel that set up a rushing touchdown by running back Christian McCaffrey. The Vikings, still adjusting to the high‑altitude conditions, managed only a field goal before the half, leaving the scoreboard at 21‑3. In the third quarter, San Francisco’s defense forced a three‑and‑out, and Purdy capped the drive with a 12‑yard touchdown pass to tight end George Kittle, extending the lead to 28‑3. The final 10 points came on a late‑game scramble by McCaffrey, sealing a comprehensive win.

Purdy’s flawless completion percentage—unprecedented for a quarterback with a minimum of 20 attempts—underscored his poise under pressure and his chemistry with the 49ers’ receiving corps. Samuel, who recorded 112 yards and a score, and Kittle, who added 78 yards and a touchdown, both highlighted the versatility of San Francisco’s passing attack. Meanwhile, McCaffrey’s 84 rushing yards and a receiving score demonstrated the dual-threat capability that has become a hallmark of the 49ers’ offense under head coach Kyle Shanahan. The team’s 425 total yards of offense eclipsed the Vikings’ 215, reflecting a stark disparity in execution and adaptability.

Minnesota, coached by former San Francisco defensive coordinator Brian Flores, entered the game with a 2‑2 record and hopes of turning the tide after a narrow loss to the New York Giants. However, the Vikings struggled to find rhythm against a relentless 49ers pass rush that recorded three sacks and forced two turnovers, including a fumble recovered by safety Jimmie Ward. Quarterback Kirk Cousins, who threw for 162 yards and a single touchdown, was repeatedly pressured, limiting his ability to establish a consistent downfield threat. The Vikings’ inability to adjust to the altitude and the 49ers’ disciplined scheme left them floundering, resulting in their worst defeat of the season.

The victory carries broader implications for the NFC West race. With the 49ers now 4‑0, they have firmly positioned themselves as the early favorite to clinch the division, while rivals such as the Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks watch closely. The win also reinforces Shanahan’s reputation for crafting game plans that exploit opponent weaknesses, a narrative that has persisted since his arrival in 2017. For the Vikings, the loss highlights the need to shore up their offensive line and develop a more adaptable defensive strategy, especially when playing in unconventional environments.

Looking ahead, the 49ers travel to Arizona for a Week 5 showdown with the Cardinals, a contest that will test whether their high‑octane offense can sustain its efficiency against a stout, home‑field defense. For Purdy, the flawless performance in Mexico City has elevated expectations; maintaining such precision will be essential if he hopes to stay in the MVP conversation as the season unfolds. Meanwhile, the Vikings must regroup quickly, focusing on protecting Cousins and re‑establishing a balanced attack, if they are to remain competitive in the tightly contested NFC North. The international stage of Mexico City may have been a brief interlude, but the ramifications of Sunday’s result will echo throughout the rest of the NFL calendar.
